sentiment: The invisible layer goes dark first, and someone quietly copies the rooms where people once asked for help.

stories.title: Quad9's withdrawal from France: A canary in the coal mine
stories.summary: A public resolver decides one country's rules are no longer workable and steps out, and almost nobody using it feels a thing. The service that answers the first question of every connection is the least visible part of the network, which is exactly why it can be withdrawn — and why the withdrawal is a warning about everything above it.

stories.title: Archive Team is archiving the Apple Support Community
stories.summary: Fifteen years of strangers diagnosing each other's broken machines is being copied before the platform turns it off. Nobody is paid for this and no institution asked for it; the volunteers do the remembering that the company has decided is no longer worth the storage. A copy is not a rescue, but it is the difference between gone and recoverable.

stories.title: Microsoft's ONNX Runtime has disappeared from GitHub
stories.summary: A repository that thousands of builds quietly point at is simply not where it was. The code is presumably fine somewhere else — but every downstream dependency that assumed a stable coordinate learns the same lesson at the same time: availability was never the same thing as presence.
